**Dark-mode primary: `#7bacfc`.** It measures OKCA 4.5 (foreground on background, against `#1a1a2e`), which meets the body-text threshold. This version costs some saturation, so you should confirm it.

The brand `#3b82f6` measures only 1.9 on `#1a1a2e`. I first tried moving lightness alone, which keeps the chroma and hue intact. That tops out at `#438aff` with contrast 2.2, so it can't reach 4.5.

Getting to 4.5 also requires reducing chroma. I ran `klar find` with `--allow-desaturation`, which gave `#7bacfc`:

| | Brand `#3b82f6` | Dark-mode `#7bacfc` |
|---|---|---|
| OKLCH lightness | 0.62 | 0.743 |
| OKLCH chroma | 0.19 | 0.128 |
| OKLCH hue | ~260° | ~260° (unchanged) |
| OKCA on `#1a1a2e` | 1.9 | **4.5** |

The hue is unchanged, but the color is lighter and less saturated, at deltaE 13 from the brand. `klar` treats trading saturation for contrast as a design decision, so it doesn't apply it unless asked. I applied it here because you asked for the closest color that passes, and it is the closest one that does.

If `#7bacfc` looks too washed out against the brand, the alternatives are to lighten the dark surface or to use the blue only for large text and UI elements. Neither is a body-text fix.

I haven't changed any files in the repo. Say so if you want me to add the token.

I couldn't produce a full 4×3 grid. `klar variants` with 4 lightness steps and 3 chroma steps returned only 3 in-gamut shades out of 12. In fixed-step mode klar divides the space evenly and doesn't check the sRGB gamut, so out-of-gamut cells come back empty.

Contrast is OKCA, shade as foreground on `#fff`. The pass threshold is 4.5 for body text.

| Lightness | C 0.078 | C 0.188 | C 0.298 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.873 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.623 | `#6b88b6` → 2.9 ❌ | `#3b82f6` → 2.9 ❌ | out of gamut |
| 0.373 | `#274069` → 9.2 ✅ | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| 0.123 | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |

- **Passes (1):** `#274069` at 9.2.
- **Fails (2):** `#6b88b6` and the base `#3b82f6`, both at 2.9. The base blue isn't usable as body text on white.
- **Out-of-gamut cells:** I didn't measure these. Contrast for an out-of-gamut colour would describe a gamut-mapped stand-in, not the colour you asked for.

Klar's adaptive mode (the default) only emits in-gamut cells, but it picks its own grid size, so you wouldn't get exactly 4×3. I can run that and pick the closest 4 lightness × 3 chroma subset if you want a fully populated grid.

I haven't measured them.

I ran every foreground in `tokens-system.json` against both backgrounds with `klar contrast` (OKCA, foreground on background, threshold 4.5). Then I used `klar find` to get a fix for each failing pair. `tokens-system.json` is unchanged.

**Results**

| Foreground | on `surface` #ffffff | on `surface-dark` #1a1a2e |
|---|---|---|
| text #1a1a2e | 15.8 ✅ | 1.0 (n/a) |
| inverse #ffffff | 1.0 (n/a) | 16.5 ✅ |
| muted #666666 | 4.8 ✅ | **2.4 ❌** |
| primary #3b82f6 | **2.9 ❌** | **1.9 ❌** |
| accent #e94560 | **2.8 ❌** | **2.0 ❌** |
| success #22c55e | **1.9 ❌** | **3.4 ❌** |

I treated `text` on dark and `inverse` on white as pairings that would never be used, since they are the same color as their background or its inverse. That is my assumption, so tell me if either should count.

**Fixes**

The fix keeps hue and changes lightness first. It reduces chroma (saturation) only when lightness alone can't reach 4.5. Those cases are marked "needs desaturation".

| Pair | Now | Proposed | OKCA | Change (ΔE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary on white | #3b82f6 (2.9) | **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15, lightness only (L 0.65→0.50) |
| accent on white | #e94560 (2.8) | **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13, lightness only |
| success on white | #22c55e (1.9) | **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22, needs desaturation (chroma 0.192→0.144) |
| muted on dark | #666666 (2.4) | **#919191** | 4.7 | 17, lightness only |
| success on dark | #22c55e (3.4) | **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5, lightness only |
| primary on dark | #3b82f6 (1.9) | **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13, needs desaturation (chroma 0.188→0.128) |
| accent on dark | #e94560 (2.0) | **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14, needs desaturation (chroma 0.199→0.141) |

- **One value per token won't work.** `primary`, `accent`, `success` and `muted` each need a darker value on white and a lighter one on dark. To fix both, split each into a light-surface and a dark-surface token, for example `primary` and `primary-on-dark`.
- **Two of the desaturation fixes are the largest changes:** `success` on white (ΔE 22) and `primary` on dark (ΔE 13). They visibly wash out the brand blue and green. I applied desaturation only because lightness alone can't reach 4.5 there.
- **`tokens.json` is separate.** The README calls it the source of truth, and it uses different, OKLCH-authored colors on white only. I didn't audit it. Some of its values, such as `success` at `oklch(0.7 0.3 150)`, look out of sRGB gamut, so it needs its own pass.

I can apply these to `tokens-system.json` or audit `tokens.json` next.
